body: This specifically affects function calls, if you instead just set the `animation` property it works, I think for these cases it's better to either use an `AnimatedSprite2D` *or* animations where you set the frame directly using just a `Sprite2D`, see [this tutorial](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/2d/2d_sprite_animation.html)

Duplicate of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/106525. Versions 4.2 and 4.3 contained a regression from 4.1 that caused erroneous seek to 0 behavior in BlendSpace. This was fixed in 4.3.1 and 4.4.

In the use case described in this issue, the problem can be resolved by using ValueTrack.

[test-blendspace2d-vtrack.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22286287/test-blendspace2d-vtrack.zip)

@TokageItLab I have a very similar problem where the function call is not triggered when setting the blend pos from the `_physics_process`. The blend pos is registered properly.

When I set the blend_pos from the UI, it works. Don't have anymore info unfort.

I can workaround this with `animation_state.travel(animation_state.get_current_node())`.

Caught me off-guard. Is this also related to the issue you mentioned?

As a side note, the suggested way just doesn't seem to scale for use cases that include sprite components. I have 13 different sprite nodes with like 80 frames. I have logic where some sprites need to be flipped, some don't. My characters have different heights, so when reusing frames I sometimes need to adjust the position. Function calls seem very essential to me, since otherwise you have a ginormous amount of logic repetition for every animation and sprite component you have.

@nihiluis I say again, seek to the start should not be performed by blending, and it was a regression bug mistakenly included in versions 4.2 and 4.3. This bug was not present in versions 4.0 and 4.1, and has been fixed in version 4.3.1 and later. > I can workaround this with animation_state.travel(animation_state.get_current_node()). State changes via StateMachine may include Reset (the Reset option for Transitions is enabled by default). Therefore, the animation is actually seeked to the start when traveling. Resetting when traveling to the same state is optional, but this is documented. In such cases where a seek to the start occurs, it is explicitly described as a "Reset". In contrast, "Blend" does not contain any meaning of “Reset”. > My characters have different heights, so when reusing frames I sometimes need to adjust the position. Function calls seem very essential to me, since otherwise you have a ginormous amount of logic repetition for every animation and sprite component you have. If you want to trigger a specific function when the animation changes, you can include it within the setter of the animation property in AnimatedSprite2D like: ```gdscript extends AnimatedSprite2D func _set(property: StringName, value) -> bool: if property == "animation" && animation != value: animation = value _on_animation_changed() return true return false func _on_animation_changed() -> void: if is_your_state_needed_adjusting: _adjust_func() ```
